title: release warmup map and checklist (personal)
content:
Context and intent:
- Personal scratchpad for the next model rollout (v3.1 -> v3.2 variant set). This is a working map: quick checklists, hypotheses to validate, run commands, and the minimal telemetry I want on the dashboard while I babysit the canary.

Goals (success criteria):
- No regression in 95th percentile token latency (target <= current + 20ms).
- Error rate for generation endpoints stays under 0.5% (5xx + 4xx that indicate runtime failures).
- Cost per 1k tokens does not spike more than 15% for the first 24 hours (we accept transient spikes during warmup).
- No functional regressions on the structured output tests (see linked eval set RW-2407).

Quick TL;DR rollout plan:
1) Pin a 1% cohort of traffic to v3.2 (canary) for 30m.
2) Observe primary signals + run targeted prompt set.
3) If green, increase to 10% for 2h with warmup-cohorts.
4) If green, 50% for 4h. Gradual to 100% depending on autopilot gates and SLOs.

Immediate checklist (preflight) — run before pinning 1%:
- [ ] Create dedicated canary route in Console: route name: canary/v3-2/personal-priya (make TTL 5m).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler policy for canary has min_replicas=2 and max_burst=1.
- [ ] Generate synthetic warmup traffic (script: tools/warmup/synth_300k_tokens.sh) and run locally against canary endpoint.
- [ ] Upload targeted eval set (RW-2407) to Optimize and stage regression alerts.
- [ ] Lock token billing alert to Slack #billing-alerts for first 6h.
- [ ] Post notice in #deployments: planned 1% canary at 09:00 PT, tagging SRE oncall.

Observability & primary signals to watch (dashboard pins):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for generation route, per-model breakdown.
- Errors: 5xx count and 4xx parsing failures (structured output).
- Token throughput: tokens/sec and avg tokens/request.
- CPU/GPU kernel errors: nvcrash logs.
- Cold-starts and KV cache hit rate (to confirm warmup efficiency).
- Billing burn-rate relative to baseline (last 24h).

Manual smoke tests to run on canary (short list):
- Sanity generation: 5 quick prompts across short/medium/long contexts. Compare latency and first-token delay.
- Structured output test: run 20 sample prompts expecting JSON schema; verify schema passes and confidence fields populated.
- Streaming behavior: open streaming session and simulate client cancellations (stop mid-stream) — check cleanup.
- Abort/Retry: simulate transient infra error (kill one replica) and observe fallback to hosted default.

Escalation thresholds (immediate rollback):
- Any sustained p95 > baseline + 100ms for > 10m.
- Error rate > 1% sustained for 15m.
- Structured output regression: > 1% schema failure on eval-set in 30m.
- Cost anomaly: burn-rate > 2x baseline during warmup window (unless expected due to synthetic warmup).

Pinning heuristics / commands (notes to self):
- Use console route pin: POST /routes/pin {route: "canary/v3-2/personal-priya", fraction: 0.01, policy: "weighted"} (double-check body keys in SDK).
- CLI quick unpin: rwctl routes unpin canary/v3-2 || rwctl routes set-fraction canary/v3-2 0.
- To force exact model variant: include header X-Redwood-Model: redwood/v3.2-q4_0 (but prefer route-level pin).

Warmup strategy notes (why we need staged warmup):
- v3.2 introduces a new KV cache eviction tweak — cold clients may see higher tail latency until cache warms.
- We need a warmup cohort (5% traffic that repeats recent requests) to prefill caches in the canary pool.
- Warmup script considerations: must spoof correct API keys / client ids to hit the same cache namespace.

Questions / unknowns to resolve (follow-ups):
- Elena: confirm whether the canary autoscaler honors kernel-level mem pressure events (I think yes but need proof).
- Marcus: do we have an A/B compare tool for streamed tokens to diff outputs? If not, run sample side-by-side and log diffs.
- SRE oncall: can we temporarily raise quota for canary project by +10% to avoid throttles during warmup?

Backout plan (rapid):
- Immediately set pin fraction to 0 and route traffic back to stable: rwctl routes set-fraction canary/v3-2 0.
- Repoint DNS route in Console fallback to redwood/v3.1-stable if any global anomaly detected.
- Run postmortem stub: tag as "rollout-abort-<timestamp>" and capture metrics, traces, and the latest nvcrash logs.

Post-rollout checks (first 24h):
- Monitor regression alerts on Optimize + per-prompt failure rates.
- Confirm model cache hit rate steady > 80% after 6h.
- Check memory and kernel error trends on all dedicated pools.
- Query top 20 slow requests and label owners for follow-up.

Notes to self: quick commands I want in my shell during rollout
- rwctl metrics tail --route canary/v3-2 --window 5m 
- rwctl logs follow --route canary/v3-2 --filter "ERROR OR nvcrash"
- tools/warmup/run_warmup.py --project canary --concurrency 50 --duration 20m

Mini experiment idea (if time allows):
- A small randomized split where 2% sees v3.2 but with quantize-low (q3) profile to compare cost/latency tradeoff quickly. If q3 is close in quality, we can use it as a fallback for burst windows.

Loose end TODOs (action items):
- [ ] Sync with Elena re: autoscaler behavior (today EOD).
- [ ] Draft short deploy note for #deployments with rollback steps and point-of-contact.
- [ ] Add the structured-output eval subset to the Optimize alert as a custom regression.
- [ ] Save warmup artifacts and sample traces to bucket: s3://redwood-deploys/warmup/2026-03-08-priya (create after run).

Quick log of the day (work journal):
- 2026-03-08 09:12 PT: sketched plan during standup, flagged RW-2407.
- 2026-03-10 11:03 PT: validated warmup script locally (minor bug in header rotation).
- 2026-03-12 08:45 PT: smoke against internal sandbox passed (p95 ~= baseline + 5ms).

Random thoughts / heuristics to keep in mind:
- Prefer route-level pins over per-request headers for long canaries (less likely to leak client behavior).
- Warmup traffic should emulate distribution of sizes: 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long to match production token mix.
- If structured outputs fail, prefer rollback; these regressions are high-risk for product correctness.

End of scratchpad — will convert to a more formal playbook if the canary goes green and we repeat this flow.

-- Priya
